Each side of the large square in the figure is trisected (divided into three equal parts). The corners of an inscribed square are at these trisection points, as shown. The ratio of the area of the inscribed square to the area of the large square is

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

A cube has eight vertices (corners) and twelve edges. A segment, such as \(x,\) which joins two vertices not joined by an edge is called a diagonal. Segment \(y\) is also a diagonal. How many diagonals does a cube have?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Each corner cube is removed from this \(3\text{ cm}\times 3\text{ cm}\times 3\text{ cm}\) cube. The surface area of the remaining figure is

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Diameter \(ACE\) is divided at \(C\) in the ratio \(2:3.\) The two semicircles, \(ABC\) and \(CDE,\) divide the circular region into an upper (shaded) region and a lower region. The ratio of the area of the upper region to that of the lower region is

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Each of the sides of five congruent rectangles is labeled with an integer, as shown. These five rectangles are placed, without rotating or reflecting, in positions \(I\) through \(V\) so that the labels on coincident sides are equal. Which of the rectangles is in position \(I?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

A square with sides of length \(1\) is divided into two congruent trapezoids and a pentagon, which have equal areas, by joining the center of the square with points on three of the sides, as shown. Find \(x,\) the length of the longer parallel side of each trapezoid.

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

A large square is divided into a small square surrounded by four congruent rectangles as shown. The perimeter of each of the congruent rectangles is \(14.\) What is the area of the large square?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

The figure shown is the union of a circle and two semicircles of diameters \(a\) and \(b,\) all of whose centers are collinear. The ratio of the area of the shaded region to that of the unshaded region is

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: Trisection gives each corner right triangle legs one-third and two-thirds of the outer side. The square-area ratio can be found either by subtracting these triangles or by finding the inner side squared.
mappings.answerReason: Normalize the outer side to 3. Each corner triangle has area 1×2/2=1, so the inner square has area 9−4=5. The requested ratio is 5/9.

mappings.rationale: Every unordered pair of vertices determines one segment. The task counts these pairs while excluding the twelve pairs that form edges; both face and space diagonals are included.
mappings.answerReason: There are C(8,2)=28 unordered vertex pairs. Subtracting the 12 edges leaves 28−12=16 diagonals.

mappings.rationale: Removing a unit corner cube removes three exposed unit faces and exposes three previously internal unit faces. Surface area is therefore preserved under each of the eight corner removals.
mappings.answerReason: The original surface area is 6×3²=54 sq. cm. Each removed corner changes the area by −3+3=0, so the remaining surface area is also 54 sq. cm.

mappings.rationale: The upper region is the large upper semicircle minus the semicircle on AC plus the semicircle on CE. The lower region uses the opposite adjustments, so semicircle areas determine the ratio.
mappings.answerReason: Take AC=2 and CE=3, so AE=5. A semicircle of diameter d has area πd²/8. The upper and lower areas are proportional to 25−4+9=30 and 25+4−9=20, giving 3:2.

mappings.rationale: Horizontal compatibility can be represented by a graph with edges E-D, D-A, and B-C. Its only three-vertex path supplies the top row; the fixed side labels determine its direction and allow the vertical matches to be checked.
mappings.answerReason: The only possible three-tile horizontal chain is E,D,A, since E's right label 7 matches D's left label and D's right label 4 matches A's left label. Placing B,C below gives vertical matches 0 and 8 and a horizontal match of 3. Thus position I contains E.

mappings.answerReason: Let the rectangle dimensions be l and w. Since 2(l+w)=14, the outer square has side l+w=7 and area 7²=49.

mappings.rationale: The shaded area is the large upper semicircle plus the semicircle of diameter a minus the semicircle of diameter b. The unshaded area has the opposite adjustments. Expanding, factoring, and cancelling simplify their ratio.
mappings.answerReason: Writing H(d)=πd²/8, the shaded area is H(a+b)+H(a)−H(b)=πa(a+b)/4. The unshaded area is H(a+b)−H(a)+H(b)=πb(a+b)/4. Their ratio is a/b.
